effective_date_basis: Section 3 says hereby revoked; complete two-page original derivative contains no delayed effectiveness. Date is the instrument's January 3 signed date; publication occurred January 13.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Express predecessor revocation is unqualified. The successor order preserves independent statutory authority, OMB functions, applicable law and appropriations; its succession exceptions do not qualify the separately enumerated predecessor revocation. Section 3(b) also strikes section 88 of EO13286 and renumbers later sections. That PARTIAL amendment is deliberately excluded from this whole-order target scope.
leads: Statutory eligibility and independent agency authority survive. Completed/accrued effects and any earlier target ending require per-target review.
Acting order itself was expressly revoked by EO14148 section2; this rule does not infer revival of predecessor or undoing of completed amendment.

legal_effect: Research lead only. Rule records an express revocation, not the first substantive cessation or an accepted target lifecycle.
quoted_clause:
Sec. 3. Revocation. (a) Executive Order 13753 of December 9, 2016 (Amending 
the Order of Succession in the Department of Homeland Security), is hereby 
revoked. 
(b) Section 88 of Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (Amendment 
of Executive Orders, and Other Actions, in Connection With the Transfer 
of Certain Functions to the Secretary of Homeland Security), is hereby 
struck in its entirety and the subsequent sections are renumbered accordingly.
